		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In November 2015, the </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">FASB</font><font style="display:inline;"> issued </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">ASU</font><font style="display:inline;"> No. 2015-17, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 740): Balance Sheet Classification of Deferred Taxes</font><font style="display:inline;">, which requires that all deferred tax assets and liabilities, along with any related valuation allowance, be classified as noncurrent in the balance sheet.&nbsp; As a result, each jurisdiction will now only have one net noncurrent deferred tax asset or liability.&nbsp; However, the new guidance does not change the existing requirement that only permits offsetting within a jurisdiction.&nbsp; Companies are still prohibited from offsetting deferred tax liabilities from one jurisdiction against deferred tax assets of another jurisdiction.&nbsp; The amendments in this accounting standard are effective for public companies for interim and annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2016, with early application permitted.&nbsp; The Company has retrospectively applied the change in accounting as of February 2, 2016.&nbsp; As such, the prior year amounts previously reported as current deferred tax assets and noncurrent deferred tax liabilities were recast and resulted in a decrease of $8.9 million, respectively, in the Consolidated Balance Sheet as of February 3, 2015.&nbsp; The change in accounting principle does not have an impact on the Company&#x2019;s results of operations, cash flows or stockholders&#x2019; equity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">87</font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">During fiscal 2012, the Company fully utilized the remaining net operating loss carryforwards generated in prior years to reduce a significant portion of federal and state current income tax requirements. Additional net operating loss carryforwards were inherited in the acquisition of MGHC Holding Corporation during fiscal 2012 and, after application of Section&nbsp;382 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 as amended, are limited to an average use of $1.8&nbsp;million per year over the next two years. The Company had approximately $3.5&nbsp;million of remaining net operating loss carryforwards at February 2, 2016 from the MGHC Holding Corporation acquisition that will begin expiring in fiscal 2029 if not utilized to offset future taxable income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has an intangible asset for the </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Mattress Firm</font><font style="display:inline;"> trade name that arose from an acquisition prior to December&nbsp;15, 2008. The intangible asset has a tax basis that generates amortization for tax purposes, for which there is no corresponding expense for financial reporting purposes since the asset has an indefinite life and is non</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;amortizable. The tax benefit from the amortization of the intangible asset, a portion which was suspended in prior year net operating losses and was realized with the utilization of net operating loss carryforwards during fiscal 2012, was recorded as a direct reduction of the financial reporting carrying value of intangible assets in the amount of $0.4&nbsp;million and $1.2&nbsp;million during fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2013, respectively. The tax benefits of this intangible asset have been fully realized as of February 3, 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Co</font><font style="display:inline;">mpany evaluates the realizability of its deferred tax assets on a quarterly basis. The Company performed an analysis of all available evidence, both positive and negative, consistent with the provisions of ASC 740</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;10</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;30</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;17 &#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Establishment of a Valuation Allowance for Deferred Tax Assets&#x201D;</font><font style="display:inline;"> and determined that it </font><font style="display:inline;">was more likely than not that the deferred tax assets would be realized for each quarterly evaluation during fiscal 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company and its subsidiaries are included in a consolidated income tax return in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and file separate income tax returns in several states. The Company and its subsidiaries settled an income tax examination of fiscal 2012 by the Internal Revenue Service during fiscal 2015.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">9. Stockholders&#x2019; Equity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Dividends</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a holding company, the ability of Mattress Firm Holding Corp. to pay dividends is limited by its ability to receive dividends or distributions from its subsidiaries. The Senior Credit Facility imposes restrictions on Mattress Holding Corp. and its subsidiary guarantors with respect to the payment of dividends to Mattress Firm Holding Corp. As of February 2, 2016, the net assets of Mattress Holding Corp. subject to such restrictions under the Senior Credit Facility was $511.4&nbsp;million. Since inception of Mattress Firm Holding&nbsp;Corp. no dividends have been paid to its stockholders.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Common Stock</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December 16, 2014, the Company completed the secondary offering of 2,512,899 shares of common stock by certain selling shareholders. The Company did not sell any shares of common stock in the offering and did not receive any proceeds from the sale. The Company incurred approximately $0.6&nbsp;million in costs related to the offering.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On April 13, 2015, the Company completed the secondary offering of 1,505,000 shares of common stock by certain selling stockholders. The Company did not sell any shares of common stock in the offering and did not receive any proceeds from the sale. The Company incurred approximately $0.5&nbsp;million in costs related to the offering.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Common Stock Reserved for Future Issuance</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As further described in Note&nbsp;14, approximately 4,206,000 shares of common stock are reserved for issuances under the 2011 Omnibus Incentive Plan. As of February 2, 2016, there were 2,200,333 shares available for future grants under the 2011 Omnibus Incentive Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Earnings per Share</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Basic net income per common share is computed by dividing the net income applicable to common shares by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted net income per common share is computed by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period, adjusted to reflect potentially dilutive securities using the treasury stock method for stock option awards. Diluted net income per common share adjusts basic net income per common share for the effects of stock options and other potentially dilutive financial instruments only in the periods in which such effect is dilutive.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">Diluted net income per common share for fiscal 2013, fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2015 excludes stock options for the purchase of 323,909, 132,719 and 92,404 shares, respectively, of common stock as their inclusion would be anti</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;dilutive. Diluted net income per common share for fiscal 2013, fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2015 excludes non</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;vested restricted stock grants of 78,465, 60,617 and 109,271 shares, respectively, as their inclusion would be anti</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;dilutive.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Certain stock option and restricted stock awards contain vesting conditions based on specified stock price targets for the Company&#x2019;s common stock as measured at each of the annual vesting dates (&#x201C;market</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;based awards&#x201D;). The Company includes such market</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;based awards in the determination of dilutive weighted average shares outstanding under the treasury stock method when, as of the date of determination, the specified stock price targets are met and the common stock shares pursuant to those awards become contingently issuable. Accordingly, the determination of diluted weighted average shares outstanding excludes, as of the date of determination, stock options for the purchase of 141,687, 15,388 and 20,896 shares of common stock for fiscal 2013, fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2015, respectively, and excludes 72,006, 144,664 and 190,029 shares of non</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;vested restricted stock for fiscal 2013, fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2015, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">10. Commitments and Contingencies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company conducts the majority of its operations from leased store and warehouse facilities pursuant to non</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;cancellable operating lease agreements with initial terms generally ranging from five to 15&nbsp;years. Certain leases include renewal options generally ranging from one to five years and contain certain rent escalation clauses. Most leases require the Company to pay its proportionate share of the property tax, insurance and maintenance expenses of the property. Certain leases provide for contingent rentals based on sales volumes; however, incremental rent expense resulting from such arrangements are accrued for those stores expected to surpass the sales threshold subject to their respective lease agreements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

No provision with respect to these investigations and actions taken or to be taken by the Company has been made in the Company&#x2019;s financial statements.</font>

Management believes the financial strength of the financial institutions minimizes the credit risk related to the Company&#x2019;s deposits.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company currently relies on Tempur Sealy and Serta Simmons as the primary suppliers of branded mattresses. Purchases of products from these manufacturers accounted for 79% of the Company&#x2019;s mattress product costs for fiscal 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Corporate Office Leases &#x2013; Rocklin, California</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">By our subsidiary, Sleep Train, we were party to two commercial lease agreements, the landlord of which is Cabernet Sunsets, LLC, a California limited liability company beneficially owned, in part, by Dale R. Carlsen, one of our directors, for the majority of fiscal 2015. The leases provided Sleep Train with office building space located at 2205 Plaza Drive, Rocklin, CA and 2204 Plaza Drive, Rocklin, CA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The terms of the leases, which were entered into years prior to our consummation of the Sleep Train acquisition, provide for ten year terms and minimum monthly rent obligations that are marginally above current market rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Annual minimum rent for fiscal year 2015 was approximately $0.5 million, in the aggregate, for both leases.&nbsp;&nbsp;Of this amount, Mr. Carlsen held an interest in approximately $0.2 million, on a gross profits basis.</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"> On September 1, 2015, Cabernet Sunsets, LLC sold the property located at 2205 Plaza Drive, Rocklin, CA to an entity that is not affiliated with Mr. Carlsen. The property located at 2204 Plaza Drive, Rocklin, CA continues to be owned by Cabernet Sunsets.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company also sponsors an executive nonqualified deferred compensation plan. Participants may elect to defer a percentage of their earned wages to the plan. The Company may, at its discretion, provide matching and profit</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;sharing contributions under this plan. The Company has not elected to make any discretionary contributions. The plan assets and related deferred compensation liability included in other assets and other noncurrent liabilities at February 3, 2015 and February 2, 201</font><font style="display:inline;">6</font><font style="display:inline;">, were approximately $1.2&nbsp;million and $1.7&nbsp;million, respectively. The plan assets are held within a rabbi trust and are restricted from Company access.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Prior to its acquisition by the Company in October 2014, Sleep Train had an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP).&nbsp;&nbsp;As part of the purchase of Sleep Train, the ESOP received cash proceeds and Company stock in exchange for the stock of Sleep Train held by the ESOP.&nbsp;&nbsp;The acquisition agreement provided that (i)&nbsp;the ESOP shall be &#x201C;frozen&#x201D; as of </font><font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">the Closing such that no new participants shall enter the plan, no further vesting credit shall accrue, and no additional contributions shall be made to the ESOP, (ii)&nbsp;all ESOP participants shall become immediately 100% vested in their accounts, (iii) all proceeds from the sale of the ESOP&#x2019;s suspense account shares shall be properly allocated in a manner permissible by the IRS and for the exclusive benefit of participants in the ESOP, and (iv)&nbsp;the ESOP shall be terminated and the entire balance of an ESOP participant&#x2019;s account shall be distributable in cash or securities as soon as administratively feasible after receipt of the IRS Approval or such earlier date as the Buyer may determine.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">2011 Omnibus Incentive Plan</font><font style="display:inline;">&#x2014;On November&nbsp;3, 2011, the Company&#x2019;s board of directors and shareholders adopted the Mattress Firm Holding Corp. 2011 Omnibus Incentive Plan to provide for the grant of equity</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;based awards to Company employees, directors and other service providers. A total of 4,206,000 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock were reserved for grants under the 2011 Omnibus Incentive Plan. There were 2,200,333 shares available for future grants under the stock incentive plan as of February 2, 2016.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Stock Options</font><font style="display:inline;">&#x2014;A portion of the stock options granted to the Company&#x2019;s employees are subject to time</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;based vesting schedules, while the remaining portion of the stock options are subject to market</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;based vesting schedules, with such vesting based on specified stock price targets. The exercise price of the options is based upon the closing market price per share of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the date of grant, and the options have a term of 10&nbsp;years.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company issued no market-based stock options in fiscal 2014 or fiscal 2015.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company bases its expected option life on the expected exercise and termination behavior of the option holders and an appropriate model of the Company&#x2019;s future stock price. The expected volatility assumption is derived from the historical volatility of similar companies&#x2019; common stock over the most recent period commensurate with the estimated expected life of the Company&#x2019;s stock options, combined with other relevant factors. The dividend yield is the annual rate of dividends per share over the exercise price of the option as of the grant date.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">For fiscal 2013, fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2015, the Company recognized $2.9&nbsp;million, $3.8&nbsp;million and $2.8&nbsp;million, respectively, of compensation expense associated with stock option awards in general and administrative expenses in the consolidated statement of operations. The Company did not capitalize any equity</font><font style="display:inline;">&#8209;based compensation costs related to stock options during fiscal 2013, fiscal 2014 and fiscal 2015.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">17. Subsequent Events</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Sleepy&#x2019;s Acquisition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On November 25, 2015, the Company entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement to purchase all of the outstanding equity interests in HMK Mattress Holdings LLC, the holding company of Sleepy&#x2019;s LLC and related entities (collectively, &#x201C;Sleepy&#x2019;s&#x201D;), for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $780 million, subject to working capital and other customary post-closing purchase price adjustments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sleepy&#x2019;s operates approximately 1,050 specialty mattress retail stores located in 17 states in the Northeast, New England, the Mid-Atlantic and Illinois and employs approximately 3,366 persons.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company completed its acquisition of Sleepy&#x2019;s on February 5, 2016, during the first week of fiscal 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the closing of the Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition, Adam Blank, Sleepy&#x2019;s chief operating officer and general counsel immediately prior to closing, became the president of Sleepy&#x2019;s. The Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition allows the Company to achieve immediate scale and presence in New England and in the Northeast where it previously had little to no presence.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The purchase price payable to the selling equityholders of HMK Mattress Holdings LLC was reduced by certain payment obligations of Sleepy&#x2019;s, including the repayment of certain indebtedness of Sleepy&#x2019;s. As described below, the Company funded a portion of the cash purchase price for the Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition by borrowing approximately $749.2 million under its Senior Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;A portion of the cash purchase price was funded, as described below, by capital that the Company raised by issuing an aggregate of 699,300 shares of its common stock to Steve Stagner, its chief executive officer at the time, and certain investment funds affiliated with J.W. Childs Associates, Inc., an existing stockholder.&nbsp;&nbsp;The remainder of the Sleepy&#x2019;s purchase price was paid by the Company, as described below, through the issuance of an aggregate of 1,062,936 shares of its common stock to certain affiliates of Adam Blank, the chief operating officer and general counsel of Sleepy&#x2019;s immediately prior to the closing of the acquisition, and Calera Capital Partners IV, L.P. (&#x201C;Calera&#x201D;) in exchange for the aggregate equity value that Mr. Blank and Calera held in HMK Mattress Holdings LLC. As noted above, the purchase price for the Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition is subject to certain post-closing adjustments, including, but not limited to, working capital adjustments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Due to the timing of the closing of the acquisition in early February 2016, the Company has not completed the work required to include all of the disclosures required by ASC 805, however, the required disclosures will be included in the Company&#x2019;s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the first quarter of its 2016 fiscal year.&nbsp;In addition, certain of the required disclosures will be included in the pro forma financial information which will be filed as an amendment to the Company&#x2019;s Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the SEC on February 5, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Amendments to Senior Credit Facility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Effective February 5, 2016, Mattress Holding Corp., the Company&#x2019;s wholly owned subsidiary (the&nbsp;&#x201C;Borrower&#x201D;), amended its then-existing senior credit facility primarily to increase the amount of available financing thereunder to be used to fund a portion of the Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition&#x2019;s cash purchase price.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In particular, the Borrower entered into Amendment No. 1 to ABL Credit Agreement (the &#x201C;ABL Amendment&#x201D;) with Mattress Holdco, Inc. (&#x201C;Holdings&#x201D;), the lenders and issuers party thereto and Barclays Bank PLC, as administrative agent and collateral agent (in such capacity, the &#x201C;ABL Agent&#x201D;), which amended the Borrower&#x2019;s then-existing $125 million asset-backed loan credit agreement dated October 20, 2014 (as amended by the ABL Amendment, the &#x201C;ABL Credit Agreement&#x201D;), among the Borrower, Holdings, the guarantor subsidiaries of the Borrower, the lenders and issuers party thereto and the ABL Agent to, among other things, increase the revolving credit commitments in favor of the Borrower thereunder by $75 million to $200 million and extend the maturity date of the facility to February 5, 2021. Approximately $104.1 million was drawn under the ABL Credit Agreement on February 5, 2016 to fund a portion of the Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition&#x2019;s cash purchase price. </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:TimesNewRoman;">Prior to the effectiveness of the ABL Amendment, the applicable margin on LIBOR rate loans under the ABL Credit Agreement varied from 1.25% to 1.75% and the applicable margin on base rate loans varied from 0.25% to 0.75%. Effective as of February 5, 2016, the applicable margin for LIBOR rate loans under the ABL Credit Agreement varies from 1.25% to 1.50% and the applicable margin for base rate loans varies from 0.25% to 0.50%.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Additionally, the Borrower entered into Amendment No. 1 to Term Loan Credit Agreement (the &#x201C;Term Loan Amendment&#x201D;) with Holdings, the lenders party thereto, and Barclays Bank PLC, as administrative agent and collateral agent (in such capacity, the &#x201C;Term Loan Agent&#x201D;), which amended the Borrower&#x2019;s then-existing $720.0 million term loan credit agreement dated October 20, 2014 (as amended by the Term Loan Amendment, the &#x201C;Term Loan Credit Agreement&#x201D;), among the Borrower, Holdings, the guarantor subsidiaries of the Borrower, the lenders party thereto, and the Term Loan Agent to, among other things, add a $665.0 million incremental term loan facility thereunder.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately $645.1 of the incremental term loan was used by the Company on February 5, 2016 to fund a portion of the Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition&#x2019;s cash purchase price. Immediately prior to the effectiveness of the Term Loan Amendment, the outstanding loans under the Term Loan Credit Agreement were subject to an interest rate of LIBOR plus 4.00% per annum, and as of February 5, 2016 bear interest at a rate of LIBOR plus 5.25%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Previously under the Term Loan Credit Agreement, loans bearing interest by reference to LIBOR had interest rates varying from 4.00% to 4.25% and loans bearing interest by reference to the base rate had interest rates varying from 3.00% to 3.25%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective as of February 5, 2016, the interest rate for all loans under the Term Loan Credit Agreement, including those previously outstanding, is LIBOR plus 5.25% for LIBOR loans and 4.25% per annum for base rate loans.</font>

Childs Associates, Inc., an existing stockholder, and Steve Stagner, its chief executive officer at the time, pursuant to which the investment funds and Mr. Stagner agreed to purchase from the Company an aggregate of 699,300 shares of its common stock at a price per share equal to $35.75 per share (which is in excess of the price at which the Company&#x2019;s common sold at the close of trading on February 2, 2016).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company completed the stock sale on February 5, 2016, concurrent with its closing of the Sleepy&#x2019;s acquisition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr. Stagner purchased 139,860 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock and the investment funds purchased, in the aggregate, 559,440 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;As noted above, the approximately $25 million in capital that the Company raised from the sale was used to fund a portion of the acquisition&#x2019;s cash purchase price.</font>
